summary: A bibliography on computer networks and data sharing, arranged into seven subject areas including data structures, description, conversion, management, security, transmission and network design. It also has an author index and updates RFC 243.

eli5.summary: A big reading list about sharing information between computers, sorted by topic.

subtitle: A 1972 reading list on sharing data between computers, sorted into seven subject areas with an author index.

tldr.problem: People designing computer networks needed to find the research on how data is described, converted, managed, secured and sent between different machines.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC is a numbered bibliography in seven lettered subject areas, followed by an index of authors that points back to entries such as B19 or G36.
tldr.outcome: It is a reference list rather than a protocol, and it updates RFC 243.

today: RFC 290 updates RFC 243. It is a snapshot of the literature as of January 1972, so it lists nothing published later.

sections.title: A Bibliography for Data Sharing
sections.content:
RFC 290 is a bibliography by Alvin P. Mullery of the Thomas J. Watson Research Center, dated January 11, 1972. It updates RFC 243.

The abstract says it is broken into seven subject areas and also contains an index of authors. Two areas, general data structures and data management, cover a very broad range, so only entries that seem especially pertinent to computer networks and data sharing are included.
sections.eli5: It is a library list. Someone collected the books and papers that matter for sharing data between computers and put them in groups.

sections.title: The Seven Subject Areas
sections.content:
The entries are grouped under lettered headings:

  • A. General data structures
  • B. Data description
  • C. Data conversion
  • D. Data management
  • E. Data security
  • F. Data transmission
  • G. Computer network design

Each entry is numbered within its area. Typical entries cite journal articles, conference papers, workshop papers and technical reports, for example a 1970 paper by E. F. Codd on a relational model of data for large shared data banks.
sections.eli5: The list has seven shelves: how data is organised, described, translated, managed, protected, sent, and how whole networks are built.

sections.title: The Author Index
sections.content:
The last part of the RFC is an author index. Each author name is followed by the codes of their entries, made of the area letter and the entry number. For example, D. P. Smith is listed under B19 and B20, and A. Weis under G36 and G39.

This lets a reader who knows a name jump straight to the matching items without scanning every area.
sections.eli5: At the back there is a list of writers. Next to each name are little codes that tell you where on the shelves to find their work.
